finding.title: Replace TierStyle.forTitle's hardcoded-English-string switch with a stable tier identifier
finding.rule: Evans (ubiquitous language / re-derived invariant) + TQ-1 (missing unit coverage)
finding.why: TierStyle.forTitle keys its visual styling entirely off the exact English milestone title string produced elsewhere (reward_milestone_service.dart's hardcoded ladder). The 7 case labels currently match, but nothing enforces that: a future rename, typo fix, or localization of a milestone title silently falls through to the generic gray `default:` style for every achievement card using that tier — no exception, no log, no test failure. grep -rln TierStyle test/ confirms there is zero test coverage anywhere in the repo pinning this mapping or the default-fallback behavior, so this class of regression would ship undetected.
finding.recommendation: Key TierStyle off a stable identifier (an enum or the milestone's stored id/threshold) rather than the display title string; add a unit test asserting each tier maps to its distinct style and that an unmatched key is either unreachable or explicitly logged.
acceptance_criteria: TierStyle.forTitle (or its replacement) takes a stable, non-localizable key instead of the raw title string.
New test/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/tier_style_test.dart asserts all 7 tiers plus the legend/default cases.

finding.title: TierStyle's ~80 hardcoded hex colors bypass the theme system and never adapt to dark mode

evidence.quote:
static ThemeData darkTheme([Color accent = brandBlueDark]) =>
      _darkTheme(accent: accent);

finding.why: TierStyle.forTitle takes no Brightness/ColorScheme parameter and returns fixed light-palette constants (cream/pastel card backgrounds, dark-on-light text) for all 8 tiers; the app has a real dark theme (AppTheme.darkTheme). A handful of entries do route through AppColors/AppTheme (e.g. AppColors.chartTeal, AppTheme.brandBlue) showing the theme system is reachable from this file, but the other ~90% of values are raw Color(0xFF...) literals. This may be an intentional 'badges always look the same' design choice, but nothing in the file states that, and if it is not intentional, achievement cards will look visually broken (light cards on a dark scaffold) whenever a user or parent switches to dark mode.
finding.recommendation: Either document that tier badges are intentionally theme-invariant, or thread Brightness/ColorScheme through TierStyle.forTitle and provide a dark variant per tier.
acceptance_criteria: Manual check (or a golden test) of the achievements screen under ThemeMode.dark confirms tier cards are legible and intentional.
If not intentional, TierStyle exposes theme-aware colors and a regression golden pins both light and dark renders.

finding.title: RewardForm is a hand-written state class with no @freezed/== override, so Riverpod can never skip a rebuild on it
finding.rule: naming/placement — 'Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes... never hand-write ==/hashCode'

evidence.quote: hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.

finding.why: RewardForm is held directly as RewardConfigController's Notifier state (per its own doc comment) but has no @freezed codegen and no == /hashCode override anywhere in the file, so it falls back to identity equality. Every copyWith() call — including a no-op one — produces a referentially distinct instance that Riverpod's default identity-based updateShouldNotify always treats as changed, so any widget watching this provider rebuilds on every field mutation regardless of whether the visible state actually changed. This is exactly the failure mode coding-standards.md cites as the reason for the @freezed rule.
finding.recommendation: Convert RewardForm to @freezed, or at minimum hand-write a field-wise == / hashCode.
acceptance_criteria: RewardForm(...) == RewardForm(...) with identical field values returns true in a new unit test.
dart analyze / build_runner clean after the freezed conversion (if chosen).

finding.title: 3 gamification test files exceed the AG-3 400-line cap
finding.why: docs/coding-standards.md's own AG-3 checker (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) explicitly scans test/ too — these are not exempt. reward_milestone_service_test.dart at 1337 lines is 3.3x the cap; see the paired 'duplicate test coverage' finding for the concrete dumping-ground cost this produced in that specific file.
finding.recommendation: Split points_service_test.dart, reward_milestone_service_extended_test.dart, and especially reward_milestone_service_test.dart along the responsibility boundaries already implied by their group() names (CRUD, unlock evaluation, cloud sync, model round-trips).
acceptance_criteria: find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' no longer lists these 3 files (or their split successors).
